name: Roadside Ambush
notes: A worked example of an encounter file - copy it to start a new one. Four adversaries against a single tier 1 PC is a losing fight by a wide margin, so the question is what softening it actually buys. The variations below move one knob each; run them together and read the comparison table. Only the party is shared: the state a fight is walked into - starting_fear, starting_spotlight, rest - belongs to the variation, and a variation that says nothing gets the ordinary opening.

variations.name: As printed
variations.notes: Every stat block exactly as the book prints it. The Sniper has 3 HP and thresholds 4/7, so it folds to almost any hit.

variations.name: Sniper toughened
variations.notes: The Sniper given enough HP to matter and enough damage to be worth fearing. Tuning it here rather than in adversaries/srd.py means the definition there still matches the book.

variations.name: One fewer bandit
variations.notes: The obvious first thing to try when a fight is too hard.

variations.name: Ambushed, no rest
variations.notes: The same opposition, walked into cold: the GM opens with the spotlight and 3 Fear, and the party arrives with nothing refreshed. The starting state is stated per variation, which is what makes this one file rather than two.
